headline: Recommended $200,000 in Housing Trust Fund money for Dorset Commons energy efficiency work, to go to City Council.
summary: Champlain Housing Trust asked for $200,000 from the Housing Trust Fund for energy efficiency work at Dorset Commons, a 105 unit family apartment property off Dorset Street. The overall project budget is $23,209,000. Members also reviewed draft Housing Trust Fund standards and plan a fuller discussion when more members are present.
decisions: Approved minutes of the last meeting, with abstentions from members who were not at that meeting.
Recommended to City Council $200,000 in Housing Trust Fund money for Dorset Commons, unanimously.

decision_titles: $200,000 in Housing Trust Funds for Dorset Commons
plain_text:
Page 1 
Housing Committee 
October 6 , 2026  
 
The South Burlington Housing Committee was called to order at 6:00 PM on October 6th 
in City Hall, 180 Market Street and via Zoom.  
Committee members present included co-Chairs Nora Senecal and Meghan Tedder, Vince 
Bolduc,  Mona Tolba (on-line) and Dawn Philibert. Committee members Sandy Dooley and 
Tasos Zois were absent. 
 
Others present: Kelsey Peterson (Senior City Planner),  Elizabeth Fitzgerald, designated 
representative from the City Council, and Javer Garcia from the Champlain Housing Trust. 
Members of the public also present were Ashley Rooks and Betty Milizia. 
 
Staff report: Kelsey did a short summary of the work of her office that may relate to the 
work of the Housing Committee and then Elizabeth Fitzgerald did a similar report of the 
work of the City Council that might relate to the housing. Shortly, she reported, the 
Council will be looking at city wide “Growth Management”  a new initiative that we should 
be aware of and perhaps plan to attend those Council meetings. The Council is also 
looking at the CCRPC state targets both on demographic growth and housing targets, 
trying to reconcile differences between them. Our Committee might be interested in 
following this discussion and adding to it if appropriate. Elizabeth also said that in her 
next column in The Other Paper, she will report on our present work on the Housing Trust 
Fund. Nora reported that she “tabeled” at the recent “Green Community” day and that 
some people stopped by to share some of their difficulties in obtaining and holding onto 
affordable housing in the community. 
 
Minutes from the last meeting were approved with abstentions from those who were not 
at the meeting.   
 
Attention then turned to a discussion of the proposal from the Champlain Housing Trust 
for $200,000 for the preservation and rehabilitation of Dorset Commons, a 105 unit family
Housing Committee July 8, 2026 | Page 2 
apartment property off Dorset Street. Quoting from the proposal: “The requested 
$200,000 in [South Burlington’s] Housing Trust Funds will support the overall budget of 
$23,209,000 to specifically allocate to the project’s energy efficiency scope.” Various 
members of our Committee agreed on the needs described for this 1970’s project and felt 
that this money would help them gain approval for a 6.25% 30 year loan for another 
$11,300,000 of the financing. The remaining budget will come from various loans, grants 
and incentives from other organizations. A draft recommendation in support of making 
this recommendation to the City Council (which had been appended to the agenda for 
tonight’s meeting) was unanimously supported by all Committee members with very 
minor edits to fully reflect the  City Council Resolution for the Housing Trust Fund (dated 
August 18, 2025). Dawn made the motion, Vince seconded it. When the motion is 
presented to the City Council we will attempt to have more members of the Housing 
Committee present, with Javer Garcia of the Champlain Housing Trust also present in case 
any questions arose. 
 
Late in the meeting, the Committee turned its attention to item 7 of the agenda on the 
“Housing Trust Fund: Discussion of Establishing Standards.” Proposed documents drafted 
by Tasos a “Core Matrix and Limits” and an “Application Scoring Rubric” had been 
included in the agenda packet, and member opinion was sought. Other than 
recommending that we delete the row on the matrix on “Emergency Rental / Utility” few 
other comments followed. Given the later hour, the Chairs asked members to give this 
draft some thought and with two other members in attendance next time, we can give 
these proposals a fair and full discussion. 
 
The Committee adjourned at 8:10. 
Respectfully submitted, 
Vince Bolduc, Secretary
